source.title: The Origins of Representation Manifolds in Large Language Models
source.authors: Alexander Modell; Patrick Rubin-Delanchy; Nick Whiteley

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representation geometry in LLMs using manifold visualizations, PCA, and rank correlations. These are different methods from toy-model superposition experiments, but bear on V6 by testing whether observed feature representations vary along manifolds rather than being fixed one-dimensional directions.
record.gate_note: The paper assumes the superposition hypothesis as background; it does not test feature sparsity, capacity competition, or the toy-model transition. Its references to prior results are not recorded as findings. Cosine-similarity and geodesic-distance results concern geometric fidelity, not feature dimensionality, so they are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study offers a theory plus LLM measurements (PCA shapes, rank correlation along kNN manifolds) showing some features are curved multi-dimensional manifolds, not single fixed directions. It argues V6 needs restating (multidimensional LRH), so T5 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also conclude that years in GPT2-small appear log-scaled and colours are encoded as a hue cycle. They argue features should be modelled as metric spaces whose representations are homeomorphic (and locally isometric) manifolds, extending the 1-D linear representation hypothesis. They describe their evidence as preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes LLM text embeddings and token activations through PCA, rank correlations, and nearest-neighbor graph distances; it does not train or sweep toy networks as in the original superposition work.
record.method_sensitivity: For the years feature, linear isometry evidence changes with the chosen metric: ordinary year distance does not fit well, while logarithmic distance does. For text embeddings, projecting onto the first few uncentered principal components is reported to help reveal plausible isometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine similarity and kNN geodesic distance track feature-space distance. Years fit a log(2019−year) metric (ξ=0.84, Pearson 0.99) but not a linear metric. Dates fit with Pearson 0.97; colours only weakly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geodesic distance on LLM representation manifolds is isometric to an intrinsic feature metric.

record.problems: The experiments are described as preliminary and use selected examples with manually proposed feature metrics. Manifold distances are estimated with K-nearest-neighbor graphs, which the authors say can suffer from short-circuits and may require manual pruning. The paper also notes that PCA can omit structure in later components.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted for the row limit.

untested.parts: How common multi-dimensional features are in LLMs; whether these manifold features are superposed with others; any non-calendar, non-colour features.
Not tested: no toy models, no sparsity transition.
Not tested: SAEs are used only as a tool to extract subspaces.
Not tested. SAE feature splitting along manifolds is only conjectured (Sec 4.2).

missing.what: Isometry tests: Chatterjee ξ and Pearson ρ for colours, years (linear metric fails, log metric 0.84/0.99) and dates (ρ 0.97).
missing.versions: none (geometry of multi-dimensional features; bears on V6 only indirectly)

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'supports' label inverted V6's direction: V6 asserts 1-D directions, and these results show multi-dimensional manifolds. Superposition itself is assumed, not tested. Text-embedding examples (R1, R4) are not internal SAE features.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more sparse features than dimensions, overlap, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular superposition geometry.
Whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study uses some SAE-derived representations but does not test feature spreading across neurons or SAE recoverability.
It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The examples are selected features and do not establish how common such representations are, whether they are superposed, or the general dimensionality of LLM features.

rows.subject: OpenAI’s text-embedding-large-3
rows.operation_detail: PCA visualization of embeddings for English color names
rows.value: The representations are roughly arranged around a loop, in hue order.
rows.note: Embeddings were reduced to three dimensions using PCA. The result bears on representations varying along a feature manifold rather than being a fixed direction.
rows.check: The reader marked this observed. Against V6, a 1-D fixed direction is not what is seen: colour embeddings form a hue-ordered loop across three PCA dimensions. Text embeddings are not SAE features, so the link to superposed features is indirect.

source_check.locator_found: Figure 1 caption; Section 2.3, colour embeddings paragraph.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: PCA visualization of SAE-extracted representations for years of the twentieth century
rows.value: The representations form a clear one-dimensional curve that bends through the space.
rows.note: The study describes a curve in the representation space, rather than a single fixed direction.
rows.check: The reader marked this observed. The years feature is a curve that is intrinsically 1-D but weaves through several dimensions, so it is not a single direction. This contradicts V6's 1-D-direction picture.

source_check.locator_found: Figure 1 caption; Section 2.3, GPT2-small year representations paragraph.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Rank association between years and their positions along a K-nearest-neighbor manifold graph
rows.measure: Rank correlations for ordering along the manifold
rows.note: The authors report that the representations occur in very close to true temporal order along the manifold.
rows.check: Kendall 0.97 and Spearman >0.99 show ordering along the manifold (homeomorphism to an interval). Such ordering would also hold for points along a linear direction, so this row alone cannot separate a 1-D direction from a curved manifold.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2.3, rank-correlation paragraph: K=10; Kendall 0.97; Spearman over 0.99.

relationships.condition: Selected continuous/cyclic features (colours, dates in text-embedding-large-3; years in GPT2-small L7; months/weekdays in Mistral 7B L8)
relationships.reason: These features occupy curved loops or curves spanning several dimensions rather than one fixed direction (R1, R2, R4, R5, R6). V6 therefore fails for this class of features; prevalence is not shown.
relationships.display_finding: These features occupy curved loops or curves spanning several dimensions rather than one fixed direction; how common such features are was not shown.

relation.reason: The study's own geometric analyses bear on V6, rather than merely using or citing superposition.

tranche.reason: The theoretical extension and empirical curved representations directly argue that fixed one-dimensional feature directions require restating.

source_check.notes: The authors describe the evidence as preliminary; calendar SAE extraction follows Engels et al. Figure 2 also uses unit normalization. Statement checks cover this study only, excluding separately attributed positional results, other studies and the catalog-wide count.
